question: What did the 1908 experiment behind the famous inverted-U curve of stress and performance actually measure?
answer: How fast mice learned to pick the brighter of two boxes under electric shocks of different strengths. For the hardest discrimination, middling shocks worked best. Nothing was measured about anxiety or people; the tidy curve linking stress to performance was drawn decades later. A study of mice and shocks became a law of the office.
move: Trace a famous curve back to what was actually measured.
ask: Which rule about how I work best, like needing pressure, have I never actually tested?
reference: Teigen, Yerkes-Dodson: A law for all seasons, Theory & Psychology, 1994
